title: Unlawful or unauthorized data collection
description: Parent user may share sensitive data (govt ID, password) without clear legal basis or consent for the intended purpose
assumptions: Assumes registration process may not have explicit legal authorization

title: Inappropriate information sharing
description: Parent user may share more personal information than necessary for authentication (e.g., government ID, six-digit code)
assumptions: Assumes user may not understand data minimization principles

title: Excessive data collection
description: Registration process collects more data than strictly necessary for authentication purposes
assumptions: Assumes authentication could be performed with fewer data elements

title: Data in transit interception
description: Sensitive data (password, govt ID) transmitted over network may be intercepted by unauthorized parties
assumptions: Assumes data may be transmitted without end-to-end encryption

title: Data integrity in transit
description: Data may be altered or corrupted during transmission between parent user and authentication service
assumptions: Assumes no integrity checks during data transmission

title: Unlawful data processing
description: Authentication service may process personal data without proper legal basis or consent
assumptions: Assumes service may not have clear legal authorization for data processing

title: Inappropriate data processing
description: Authentication service may use collected data for purposes beyond authentication (e.g., marketing, profiling)
assumptions: Assumes service may have broader data usage policies than stated

title: Unnecessary data retention
description: Authentication service may retain more personal data than necessary for service provision
assumptions: Assumes service may not implement data minimization practices

title: Unintended data use
description: Authentication service may use collected data for purposes other than stated authentication purpose
assumptions: Assumes service may have undisclosed data usage practices

title: Unauthorized disclosure of parent account data
description: Parent account information stored in MongoDB users collection could be accessed by unauthorized parties through data breach, misconfiguration, or insider threats, leading to potential identity theft or privacy violations.
assumptions: MongoDB access controls are properly configured and monitored

title: Identification of users through parent account sharing
description: The authentication service shares parent account information that can be used to identify and link individual users, potentially enabling profiling or targeted actions against specific individuals.
assumptions: Parent account data contains personally identifiable information

title: Linkability through data flow metadata
description: Data in transit between authentication service and MongoDB could contain metadata that links users together, enabling correlation of activities across different data flows or systems.
assumptions: Data flow metadata is not properly encrypted or anonymized

title: Unintended use of parent account data
description: Parent account information stored in MongoDB may be accessed or used for purposes other than the intended authentication and account management functions, such as marketing, analytics, or third-party sharing.
assumptions: Data access controls and usage policies are comprehensive

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: Storing parent account information may violate privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, COPPA, CCPA) regarding consent, data minimization, and purpose limitation for personal data of children or parents.
assumptions: Applicable privacy regulations require specific consent and handling procedures

title: Unauthorized JWT Disclosure at Source
description: Authentication service may share JWT tokens with insufficient access controls, potentially allowing unauthorized parties to intercept or access authentication credentials during the sharing process.

title: Excessive User Data Sharing
description: Authentication service may share more user data than necessary for authentication purposes, violating data minimization principles.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: JWT and user data in transit may be intercepted by unauthorized parties if transmission is not properly encrypted or protected.

title: Unintended User Data Exposure
description: Parent User may receive unintended or excessive user data beyond what is necessary for authentication, potentially leading to privacy concerns.

title: Data Integrity Concerns at Destination
description: Parent User may receive corrupted or tampered user data during the authentication process, affecting the accuracy and reliability of the information.

title: Unauthorized sharing of parent credentials
description: Child user may share parent email and password without proper legal authority or consent, potentially violating data protection laws regarding minors' data

title: Informed consent not obtained
description: Child may not fully understand the implications of sharing parent authentication credentials, lacking proper informed consent

title: Data interception during authentication
description: Parent email and password in transit could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, exposing sensitive authentication credentials

title: Excessive data retention
description: Authentication service may retain more data than necessary for authentication purposes, including unnecessary parent email information

title: Inadequate data protection
description: Authentication service may not adequately protect credentials during storage and processing, increasing risk of unauthorized access

title: Lawful basis for sharing child profile data
description: Authentication service may be sharing child profile data without proper legal basis or consent from the child user or their guardians.
assumptions: Assumes child profile data contains sensitive personal information

title: Inaccurate or incomplete JWT token data
description: JWT tokens may contain inaccurate, outdated, or incomplete child profile information that could lead to misidentification or incorrect user experience.
assumptions: Assumes JWT tokens are generated from potentially stale or incorrect source data

title: Data integrity during JWT transmission
description: JWT tokens containing child profile data could be intercepted, modified, or tampered with during transmission from authentication service to child user.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over potentially insecure channels

title: Unintended disclosure of child profile information
description: Sensitive child profile data embedded in JWT tokens could be exposed to unauthorized parties during data transmission.
assumptions: Assumes JWT tokens may be intercepted by third parties

title: Purpose limitation by child user
description: Child user may use the JWT tokens and profile data for purposes beyond the intended authentication or service access.
assumptions: Assumes child user has access to the JWT tokens and profile data

title: Misuse of received profile data
description: Child user may misuse the received child profile data for purposes other than intended authentication or service access.
assumptions: Assumes child user has access to and can manipulate the profile data

title: Lawful basis for sharing child data
description: Parent may share child profile information without proper legal basis or consent from the child (if old enough to consent) or appropriate guardianship verification.
assumptions: Parent may not have proper legal authority or consent documentation

title: Excessive data sharing
description: Parent may share more child data than necessary for profile creation, including sensitive government ID information that could be used for identity theft.
assumptions: Parent may not understand data minimization principles

title: Data integrity during transmission
description: Child profile data in transit may be altered, corrupted, or tampered with during transmission from parent to profile management system.
assumptions: Data may traverse multiple networks or systems

title: Unintended interception of child data
description: Sensitive child information (name, DOB, govt ID) in transit may be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission.
assumptions: Data may traverse public or unsecured networks

title: Lawful processing of child data
description: Child Profile Management process may process child data without proper legal basis or compliance with child privacy regulations.
assumptions: Process may not have proper legal framework for child data processing

title: Data retention beyond necessity
description: Child profile data may be retained longer than necessary for the intended purpose, increasing exposure risk.
assumptions: Process may not have data retention policies

title: Unintended access to stored child profiles
description: Child profile data stored in the process may be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems.
assumptions: Process may not have adequate access controls

title: Data Integrity - Profile Data Corruption
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could be corrupted, altered, or tampered with during storage, leading to inaccurate or misleading information about children.
assumptions: Assumes MongoDB storage mechanisms are properly configured and protected against unauthorized modifications.

title: Data Availability - Profile Access Unavailability
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could become inaccessible due to system failures, attacks, or maintenance issues, preventing authorized users from accessing critical information.
assumptions: Assumes MongoDB service is continuously available and protected against denial-of-service attacks.

title: Data Confidentiality - Unauthorized Access to Profiles
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could be accessed by unauthorized parties due to security vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, or breaches, exposing sensitive personal information about children.
assumptions: Assumes MongoDB access controls are properly configured and enforced.

title: Data Accuracy - Profile Information Inaccuracy
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could be inaccurate or incomplete due to input errors, system limitations, or lack of validation mechanisms, leading to incorrect information about children.
assumptions: Assumes data validation and verification processes are implemented.

title: Data Retention - Excessive Profile Data Retention
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could be retained longer than necessary, increasing privacy risks and potential exposure of sensitive personal information about children.
assumptions: Assumes data retention policies are properly implemented and enforced.

title: Data Linkage - Profile Data Correlation
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could be linked with other datasets or metadata, potentially enabling re-identification or profiling of children beyond the intended scope.
assumptions: Assumes MongoDB does not automatically link data with external sources.

title: Child User Identification Risk
description: Child user's search patterns, likes, and comments may be used to identify or profile the child beyond their stated identity, potentially violating child privacy protections.
assumptions: Assumes child user may not fully understand the implications of their data sharing

title: Insufficient Notification to Child User
description: Child user may not be adequately informed about what data is being shared, how it will be used, or with whom it will be shared during video search, request, like, and comment activities.
assumptions: Assumes child user may lack full understanding of privacy implications

title: Potential Non-Compliance with Child Privacy Laws
description: Sharing of child user data may not comply with applicable child privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) regarding consent, data collection limits, and parental involvement.
assumptions: Assumes jurisdiction may have specific child privacy requirements

title: Video Management Service User Identification
description: Video management service may identify or link the child user through their search history, likes, comments, and other behavioral data, creating persistent profiles.
assumptions: Assumes service maintains user accounts and tracking mechanisms

title: Insufficient Notification to Child User at Destination
description: Child user may not be adequately notified about how their data is processed, stored, and used by the video management service after receipt.
assumptions: Assumes service may have privacy policies that are not clearly communicated to children

title: Inadequate Data Destruction for Child Data
description: Child user data may not be properly destroyed when no longer needed or when account is terminated, potentially leading to long-term privacy risks.
assumptions: Assumes service may retain data beyond necessary retention periods

title: Unintended Consequences of Data Processing
description: Processing of child user data (search, likes, comments) may have unintended consequences such as algorithmic profiling, targeted advertising, or data breaches affecting the child.
assumptions: Assumes service may have complex data processing systems with potential side effects

title: Data Flow Meta-Data Identification Risk
description: Meta-data about the parties (child user and video service) in the data flow may be used to link or identify the child user, even without explicit content data.
assumptions: Assumes network-level or service-level metadata may be captured and analyzed

title: Lack of Notice for Video Data Collection
description: Users may not be adequately informed about what video metadata and files are being collected, how they are used, and with whom they are shared.
assumptions: Assumes users expect to be notified about data collection practices.

title: Excessive Data Collection
description: The Video Management Service may collect more video metadata and files than necessary for the stated purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Assumes the service collects all available video data without strict necessity criteria.

title: Potential Lawfulness Issues
description: The collection and sharing of video metadata and files may not have a clear legal basis or may violate applicable privacy regulations.
assumptions: Assumes the service operates without explicit legal authorization for all data processing activities.

title: Excessive Data Retention
description: The MongoDB collection may retain video metadata and files longer than necessary, increasing privacy risks and violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Assumes the data store retains data without defined retention policies.

title: Unintended Consequences of Data Storage
description: Storing video metadata and files in MongoDB may have unintended privacy consequences, such as enabling re-identification or linking across datasets.
assumptions: Assumes the data store may be accessed or linked with other data sources.

title: Non-compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: The MongoDB data store may not comply with applicable privacy regulations regarding data storage, access controls, and user rights.
assumptions: Assumes the data store operates without comprehensive privacy compliance measures.

title: Lawful basis for collecting child search and watch history unclear
description: The collection of child search and watch history may lack a clear lawful basis under privacy regulations, especially given the sensitive nature of child data.
assumptions: Assumes no explicit legal framework or consent mechanism is documented for this data collection.

title: Excessive data collection for child profile
description: Collecting comprehensive search and watch history may be more extensive than necessary for the stated purpose of child profile management, potentially violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Assumes the purpose is limited to basic child profile management.

title: Insufficient notification to parents/guardians
description: Parents or guardians may not be adequately informed about what data is being collected, how it will be used, and their rights regarding this data.
assumptions: Assumes standard privacy notification practices may not be fully implemented.

title: Inadequate data retention and destruction policies
description: Child search and watch history may be retained indefinitely without clear retention schedules or secure destruction procedures, increasing long-term privacy risks.
assumptions: Assumes no documented data retention policy exists for this data store.

title: Data stored in potentially insecure manner
description: MongoDB childprofiles collection may not have appropriate security controls (encryption, access controls) to protect child search and watch history from unauthorized access.
assumptions: Assumes standard MongoDB security may not be sufficient for sensitive child data.

title: Potential non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Storage and handling of child search and watch history may not comply with specific child privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) which have stricter requirements for child data.
assumptions: Assumes no specific child privacy compliance framework has been implemented.

title: Unintended Disclosure of Video Content
description: Parent user may upload video content that contains sensitive personal information (e.g., children, private conversations) without proper consent or awareness of potential exposure.
assumptions: User may not fully understand privacy implications of video upload

title: Identification of User Through Video Metadata
description: Video upload may include metadata (timestamps, location, device info) that could be used to identify or track the parent user.
assumptions: Video files contain embedded metadata

title: Unintended Disclosure During Data Transmission
description: Video data in transit may be intercepted or exposed during upload, potentially revealing content to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be fully encrypted or may occur over insecure channels

title: Unintended Disclosure by Video Management Service
description: Video Management Service may disclose video content to unauthorized parties, including third-party advertisers, law enforcement without proper authorization, or other users.
assumptions: Service may have access to video content and may share it without proper consent

title: Identification of Users Through Video Processing
description: Video Management Service may identify users through video content analysis, facial recognition, or behavioral tracking during approval/rejection process.
assumptions: Service may employ automated or manual identification techniques

title: Non-compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: Video Management Service may process video data in ways that violate applicable privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, COPPA) regarding consent, data retention, or user rights.
assumptions: Service may not have adequate privacy compliance measures

title: Video Content Tampering at Source
description: The Video Management Service may not ensure the integrity of video content before sharing, potentially allowing unauthorized modifications or tampering with the video stream.
assumptions: Assumes the service has some control over video content before transmission

title: Lawful Basis for Video Sharing
description: The Video Management Service may lack a clear lawful basis for sharing video content with the child, potentially violating data protection principles.
assumptions: Assumes the service operates under some data protection framework

title: Video Stream Interception in Transit
description: Video data in transit may be intercepted or modified by unauthorized parties, compromising the integrity of the streaming content.
assumptions: Assumes the data flow is not fully encrypted or protected

title: Unintended Consequences of Video Viewing
description: The child user may experience unintended consequences from viewing the video content, such as inappropriate exposure or psychological impact.
assumptions: Assumes the child may not fully understand or be prepared for the content

title: Child Modifying Video Content
description: The child user may modify or alter the video content after receipt, potentially changing the original message or content.
assumptions: Assumes the child has technical capability to modify the video

title: Unlawful collection of child browsing data
description: Child browsing data may be collected without proper parental consent or legal basis, violating data protection laws for minors. The source element (MongoDB childprofiles collection) may be sharing data without adequate legal foundation.
assumptions: Assuming this is a planned implementation without established consent mechanisms for child data collection.

title: Inappropriate profiling of children
description: The AI Recommendation Engine will create profiles of children based on browsing data, potentially leading to inappropriate inferences about minors' interests, behaviors, or characteristics without proper safeguards.
assumptions: Assuming the AI engine will use browsing data for profiling and recommendation purposes.

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Child browsing data in transit between MongoDB and AI engine could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, exposing sensitive information about children's browsing behavior.
assumptions: Assuming data is transmitted without end-to-end encryption or adequate security measures.

title: Data used beyond original purpose
description: Child browsing data may be used for purposes other than the originally stated purpose of AI recommendations, potentially including commercial profiling or targeted advertising without additional consent.
assumptions: Assuming the AI engine may repurpose data without additional consent mechanisms.

title: Excessive data retention of child information
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may retain child browsing data longer than necessary, increasing the risk of future data breaches and violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Assuming the AI engine will store browsing data for extended periods for future recommendations.

title: Unlawful sharing of browsing data with third-party advertisers
description: Users may not have given informed consent for their browsing data to be shared with third-party advertisers. The sharing of browsing data to advertisers may violate data protection laws requiring lawful basis for processing personal data.
assumptions: Assuming browsing data contains personal information about users' browsing behavior

title: Insufficient notice to users about data sharing with advertisers
description: Users may not be adequately informed about what browsing data is being collected and shared with third-party advertisers. Privacy policies may not clearly disclose this data flow.
assumptions: Assuming users are expected to review privacy policies

title: Data disclosure during transmission to advertisers
description: Browsing data in transit from AI Recommendation Engine to third-party advertisers could be intercepted, exposed, or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission.
assumptions: Assuming data is transmitted over networks that may not be fully secured

title: Unintended processing of browsing data by advertisers
description: Third-party advertisers may process browsing data for purposes beyond advertising, such as profiling, selling data, or using it for purposes not disclosed to users.
assumptions: Assuming advertisers have discretion over how they use received data

title: Further disclosure of browsing data by advertisers
description: Third-party advertisers may share browsing data with other entities without user consent, potentially leading to broader data exposure than intended.
assumptions: Assuming advertisers may have business relationships with other data processors

title: Excessive Data Collection
description: Authentication Service may collect more government ID images than necessary for authentication purposes, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Assumes the service collects all ID images without filtering based on necessity.

title: Potential Lawfulness Issues
description: The collection and sharing of government ID images may lack clear legal basis or proper consent from data subjects.
assumptions: Assumes the service operates without explicit legal authorization for this data handling.

title: Insufficient Notice Provision
description: Users may not be adequately informed about what government ID images are being collected, why, and how they will be used.
assumptions: Assumes the service does not provide clear privacy notices to users.

title: Metadata Exposure During Transmission
description: Data flow may expose metadata about the parties involved (e.g., timestamps, file names, headers) that could be used to link or identify individuals.
assumptions: Assumes standard file transmission protocols that may leak metadata.

title: Unintended Access to Stored Images
description: Stored government ID images may be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: Assumes the file system lacks adequate access controls.

title: Inadequate Data Minimization at Storage
description: The file system may store government ID images without proper retention policies or deletion mechanisms, leading to unnecessary data accumulation.
assumptions: Assumes the storage system lacks automated retention and deletion policies.

title: Potential Non-Compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: Storage of government ID images may not comply with applicable privacy laws and regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA, or national privacy laws).
assumptions: Assumes the storage practices may not meet all legal requirements.

title: JWT Exposure via XSS Attack
description: JWT tokens stored in browser localStorage can be exposed through Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks, allowing malicious scripts to read and exfiltrate the token data.
assumptions: Assumes browser localStorage is accessible to scripts and XSS vulnerabilities may exist in the application or third-party scripts.

title: Unauthorized Access to LocalStorage
description: Any user or malicious actor with access to the browser instance can access the localStorage, potentially stealing JWT tokens without authentication.
assumptions: Assumes no additional security controls (like secure storage APIs) are in place to protect the localStorage.

title: User Session Linkage via JWT
description: JWT tokens contain user identifiers that can be used to link user sessions across different contexts, devices, or time periods, potentially enabling session hijacking or profiling.
assumptions: Assumes JWT contains user-identifying information that can be correlated across sessions.

title: JWT Loss via Browser Clear
description: If the user clears browser history or cache, or if the browser is reset, the JWT stored in localStorage may be lost, potentially requiring re-authentication and disrupting user experience.
assumptions: Assumes users may clear browser data or browsers may be reset.

title: Unlawful or Unauthorized Sharing of Child History Data
description: The Child Profile Management process may share child history data without proper legal basis, consent from the child (if of age), or appropriate parental authorization.
assumptions: Assumes child history data is sensitive personal information requiring proper legal basis for sharing.

title: Excessive Data Collection and Sharing
description: The process may retrieve and share more child history data than necessary for the parent review purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Assumes the process has discretion over what data to retrieve.

title: Inaccurate or Incomplete Child History Data
description: The child history data retrieved may contain errors, omissions, or outdated information that could mislead the parent in their review.
assumptions: Assumes the data source may have quality control issues.

title: Unintended Disclosure During Data Transmission
description: Child history data in transit may be intercepted by unauthorized parties through network vulnerabilities or man-in-the-middle attacks.
assumptions: Assumes the data transmission channel may not be fully secured.

title: Unauthorized Sharing of Retrieved Child History
description: The parent user may share the retrieved child history data with unauthorized third parties or use it for purposes beyond the intended review.
assumptions: Assumes the parent may not be bound by appropriate privacy obligations.

title: Inadequate Data Destruction After Review
description: The parent may retain child history data beyond the intended retention period or fail to properly delete it after review.
assumptions: Assumes the parent may not follow proper data retention practices.
